concepts.name: Optogenetic stimulation
concepts.rationale: Core intervention; optogenetics is a modern method that is well covered by MeSH but many tool-specific terms (ChR2, opsin variants) require free-text.

concepts.name: Hippocampus
concepts.rationale: Anatomical target of stimulation; subregions and engram-cell jargon add recall.

concepts.name: Memory consolidation
concepts.rationale: Primary outcome; consolidation is a specific process but related learning/memory paradigms and LTP mechanisms broaden recall.

concepts.name: Rodent model
concepts.rationale: Population/model constraint; optogenetics is almost always transgenic-line dependent so Cre/driver terms help.

map.notes: The 'improve' (directional effect) is not made a separate block to preserve recall; effect direction is best assessed at screening. Consolidation and general learning/memory overlap substantially, so the Memory block is intentionally broad. Consider whether to exclude purely mechanistic LTP-only studies at screening if the question is behavioral. If only rodents are of interest, the Rodent block can be ANDed; otherwise drop it to capture reviews and methods papers.

concepts.name: Optogenetic stimulation
concepts.rationale: Core intervention; optogenetics is a modern method that is well covered by MeSH but many tool-specific terms (ChR2, opsin variants) require free-text.

concepts.name: Hippocampus
concepts.rationale: Anatomical target of stimulation; subregions and engram-cell jargon add recall.

concepts.name: Memory consolidation
concepts.rationale: Primary outcome; consolidation is a specific process but related learning/memory paradigms and LTP mechanisms broaden recall.

concepts.name: Rodent model
concepts.rationale: Population/model constraint; optogenetics is almost always transgenic-line dependent so Cre/driver terms help.

map.notes: The 'improve' (directional effect) is not made a separate block to preserve recall; effect direction is best assessed at screening. Consider whether to exclude purely mechanistic LTP-only studies at screening if the question is behavioral. If only rodents are of interest, the Rodent block can be ANDed; otherwise drop it to capture reviews and methods papers.

concepts.name: Single-cell RNA sequencing
concepts.rationale: Core methodology block. MeSH indexing of scRNA-seq is inconsistent and recent, so heavy free-text coverage of abbreviations and both cell- and nucleus-based variants is essential; snRNA-seq is especially common for frozen brain tissue.

concepts.name: Microglia
concepts.rationale: Population/cell-type block. Includes canonical MeSH plus current jargon such as 'disease-associated microglia (DAM)' and marker genes used to define/annotate microglial clusters in single-cell studies.

concepts.name: Alzheimer's disease
concepts.rationale: Disease/condition block. 'AD' abbreviation and amyloid/tau terms capture studies framed around pathology; note 'AD' is ambiguous (atopic dermatitis, autosomal dominant) and should be combined with other blocks to reduce noise.

map.notes: Three blocks ANDed together (method AND cell type AND disease). Recall-oriented: many valid single-cell microglia papers may only mention scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq in the abstract, not as MeSH, so free-text is critical. Consider whether to include mouse models (5xFAD, APP/PS1, 3xTg) — currently mouse-model terms are folded implicitly via disease terms but could be added as a supplementary block if animal studies are in scope. The abbreviation 'AD' and 'DAM' are ambiguous and gain specificity only through block combination. Spatial transcriptomics and CITE-seq are included as adjacent single-cell methods; drop them if strictly limiting to RNA-only single-cell approaches.

concepts.name: Single-cell RNA sequencing
concepts.rationale: Core methodology block. MeSH indexing of scRNA-seq is inconsistent and recent, so heavy free-text coverage of abbreviations and both cell- and nucleus-based variants is essential; snRNA-seq is especially common for frozen brain tissue.

concepts.name: Microglia
concepts.rationale: Population/cell-type block. Includes canonical MeSH plus current jargon such as 'disease-associated microglia (DAM)' and marker genes used to define/annotate microglial clusters in single-cell studies.

concepts.name: Alzheimer's disease
concepts.rationale: Disease/condition block. 'AD' abbreviation and amyloid/tau terms capture studies framed around pathology; note 'AD' is ambiguous (atopic dermatitis, autosomal dominant) and should be combined with other blocks to reduce noise.

map.notes: Three blocks ANDed together (method AND cell type AND disease). Recall-oriented: many valid single-cell microglia papers may only mention scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq in the abstract, not as MeSH, so free-text is critical. Consider whether to include mouse models (5xFAD, APP/PS1, 3xTg) — currently mouse-model terms are folded implicitly via disease terms but could be added as a supplementary block if animal studies are in scope. The abbreviation 'AD' and 'DAM' are ambiguous and gain specificity only through block combination. Spatial transcriptomics and CITE-seq are included as adjacent single-cell methods; drop them if strictly limiting to RNA-only single-cell approaches.

concepts.name: Population/Model
concepts.rationale: The research question specifies rodent models. MeSH terms cover the major taxonomic groups and the concept of animal disease models, which is often used for experimental models. Freetext includes singular/plural forms and common lab jargon.

concepts.name: Intervention/Stimulation
concepts.rationale: The core intervention is optogenetic stimulation. 'Optogenetics' is the primary MeSH term. Freetext includes the intervention name, key tools (opsins like ChR2), related techniques (fiber photometry), and both excitatory and inhibitory variants to be comprehensive.

concepts.name: Anatomical Target
concepts.rationale: The stimulation target is explicitly the hippocampus. The MeSH term is precise. Freetext includes the adjective form, major subfields (CA1, DG), and closely associated structures (entorhinal cortex, hippocampal formation) to capture studies focusing on specific hippocampal circuits.

concepts.name: Outcome/Process
concepts.rationale: The primary outcome is memory consolidation. MeSH has a specific descriptor. Freetext includes the process name, related memory stages (encoding, retrieval), key cellular models (LTP, STDP), and contemporary concepts (engram) that are often measured as proxies for consolidation.

map.notes: The search strategy focuses on the causal link between stimulation and consolidation. It may also retrieve studies on inhibition or other memory processes. The outcome block is broad to capture various measures of consolidation (behavioral, electrophysiological, molecular). The intervention and target blocks are tightly coupled; combining them with 'AND' is crucial to isolate hippocampal optogenetics studies. Some relevant studies might use broader terms like 'neural stimulation' or 'deep brain stimulation' without specifying 'optogenetics', but including those would introduce excessive noise. The strategy assumes 'improve' is implied by the outcome measures and does not require a separate comparator block.

concepts.name: Population/Model
concepts.rationale: The research question specifies rodent models. MeSH terms cover the major taxonomic groups and the concept of animal disease models, which is often used for experimental models. Freetext includes singular/plural forms and common lab jargon.

concepts.name: Intervention/Stimulation
concepts.rationale: The core intervention is optogenetic stimulation. 'Optogenetics' is the primary MeSH term. Freetext includes the intervention name, key tools (opsins like ChR2), related techniques (fiber photometry), and both excitatory and inhibitory variants to be comprehensive.

concepts.name: Anatomical Target
concepts.rationale: The stimulation target is explicitly the hippocampus. The MeSH term is precise. Freetext includes the adjective form, major subfields (CA1, DG), and closely associated structures (entorhinal cortex, hippocampal formation) to capture studies focusing on specific hippocampal circuits.

concepts.name: Outcome/Process
concepts.rationale: The primary outcome is memory consolidation. MeSH has a specific descriptor. Freetext includes the process name, related memory stages (encoding, retrieval), key cellular models (LTP, STDP), and contemporary concepts (engram) that are often measured as proxies for consolidation.

map.notes: The search strategy focuses on the causal link between stimulation and consolidation. It may also retrieve studies on inhibition or other memory processes. The outcome block is broad to capture various measures of consolidation (behavioral, electrophysiological, molecular). The intervention and target blocks are tightly coupled; combining them with 'AND' is crucial to isolate hippocampal optogenetics studies. Some relevant studies might use broader terms like 'neural stimulation' or 'deep brain stimulation' without specifying 'optogenetics', but including those would introduce excessive noise. The strategy assumes 'improve' is implied by the outcome measures and does not require a separate comparator block.

concepts.name: Methodological Focus (Detection & Analysis)
concepts.rationale: Exhaustive capture of methods and tools for finding and analyzing off-target sites. Includes both experimental assays (GUIDE-seq, etc.) and computational/bioinformatic approaches. MeSH terms cover broad categories, while freetext includes specific technique names and current jargon.

map.notes: The search is designed for high recall on methods to detect CRISPR-Cas9 off-target effects. A key challenge is that many detection methods (e.g., GUIDE-seq) are relatively new and may not have dedicated MeSH terms; they are captured via freetext. The 'Methodological Focus' block is intentionally broad to encompass both experimental and computational strategies. Searches may also retrieve articles on off-target detection for other gene-editing technologies (e.g., TALENs, ZFNs), which is acceptable for a comprehensive review of methods potentially applicable to CRISPR-Cas9.

concepts.name: Optogenetic stimulation
concepts.rationale: Captures the experimental manipulation of using light-activated opsins to stimulate neural tissue. Includes current jargon and gene/protein tool terms commonly used in titles and abstracts.

concepts.name: Hippocampus
concepts.rationale: Focuses the anatomical target to hippocampal structures and subregions often reported in rodent optogenetics studies.

concepts.name: Memory consolidation
concepts.rationale: Targets the outcome of improved consolidation/retention. Includes broader memory-learning terminology and engram language frequently used in current neuroscience literature.

concepts.name: Rodent model
concepts.rationale: Restricts to rodent experimental models, including mice and rats, which are the most common systems for hippocampal optogenetics and memory studies.

map.notes: Consider whether to include an additional concept block for 'behavioral memory tasks' if you want to enrich recall for studies that assess consolidation via task performance (e.g., fear conditioning, spatial memory, Morris water maze). 'Neuronavigation' is not a relevant MeSH term here and would typically be omitted from a final strategy. For exhaustive searching, use both MeSH and title/abstract terms, and consider adjacency operators for phrases like optogenetic* and memory consolidation.

concepts.name: rodent models
concepts.rationale: Ensures inclusion of all rodent species commonly used in neuroscience research, including transgenic and genetically modified variants, while avoiding human-specific terms.

concepts.name: hippocampus optogenetic stimulation
concepts.rationale: Captures all optogenetic techniques targeting the hippocampus, including channelrhodopsins and halorhodopsins, as well as broader optogenetic tools and methods. Ensures inclusion of both activation and inhibition studies.

concepts.name: memory consolidation
concepts.rationale: Covers a broad range of terms related to memory consolidation, including both behavioral and neural processes, to ensure a high recall of studies investigating this outcome in the context of optogenetic stimulation.

concepts.name: systematic review methodology
concepts.rationale: This block is not strictly a PICO concept but is critical for ensuring the search strategy is reproducible and aligns with systematic review standards. It ensures that the search strategy can be replicated by others for consistency and rigor.

map.notes: {'scope': 'Focuses strictly on rodent models and optogenetic interventions in the hippocampus. Excludes human studies, non-optogenetic memory interventions, and studies outside the hippocampus.', 'ambiguity': {'optogenetic': 'Ensure studies explicitly mention optogenetic stimulation (not just photostimulation or laser-based methods unless optogenetic-specific tools are used).', 'memory consolidation': 'Includes both behavioral and neural measures of memory consolidation. Ensure studies explicitly link optogenetic stimulation to memory consolidation (e.g., behavioral tasks like spatial memory, fear conditioning, or object recognition).', 'hippocampus': 'Confirms that the intervention is specifically targeting the hippocampus rather than other brain regions. Use anatomical specificity in free-text terms.'}, 'reproducibility': {'sensitivity': 'Prioritize free-text terms to maximize recall of studies not yet indexed by MeSH, especially in emerging optogenetic and memory fields.', 'specificity': 'Use MeSH terms for core concepts to ensure precision in indexing.', 'combination': 'Combine MeSH and free-text terms with OR for each concept block and AND between blocks to balance sensitivity and specificity.'}, 'additional_caveats': {'timeframe': 'Consider limiting to recent years (e.g., post-2010) given the rapid evolution of optogenetic tools and memory research.', 'animal models': 'Explicitly exclude studies using non-rodent models (e.g., non-mammalian species) unless specified otherwise.', 'human studies': 'Exclude human studies unless the question explicitly includes them, as optogenetic techniques are not yet widely used in humans.'}}

concepts.name: rodent models
concepts.rationale: Ensures inclusion of all rodent species commonly used in neuroscience research, including transgenic and genetically modified variants, while avoiding human-specific terms.

concepts.name: hippocampus optogenetic stimulation
concepts.rationale: Captures all optogenetic techniques targeting the hippocampus, including channelrhodopsins and halorhodopsins, as well as broader optogenetic tools and methods. Ensures inclusion of both activation and inhibition studies.

concepts.name: memory consolidation
concepts.rationale: Covers a broad range of terms related to memory consolidation, including both behavioral and neural processes, to ensure a high recall of studies investigating this outcome in the context of optogenetic stimulation.

concepts.name: systematic review methodology
concepts.rationale: This block is not strictly a PICO concept but is critical for ensuring the search strategy is reproducible and aligns with systematic review standards. It ensures that the search strategy can be replicated by others for consistency and rigor.

map.notes: {'scope': 'Focuses strictly on rodent models and optogenetic interventions in the hippocampus. Excludes human studies, non-optogenetic memory interventions, and studies outside the hippocampus.', 'ambiguity': {'optogenetic': 'Ensure studies explicitly mention optogenetic stimulation (not just photostimulation or laser-based methods unless optogenetic-specific tools are used).', 'memory consolidation': 'Includes both behavioral and neural measures of memory consolidation. Ensure studies explicitly link optogenetic stimulation to memory consolidation (e.g., behavioral tasks like spatial memory, fear conditioning, or object recognition).', 'hippocampus': 'Confirms that the intervention is specifically targeting the hippocampus rather than other brain regions. Use anatomical specificity in free-text terms.'}, 'reproducibility': {'sensitivity': 'Prioritize free-text terms to maximize recall of studies not yet indexed by MeSH, especially in emerging optogenetic and memory fields.', 'specificity': 'Use MeSH terms for core concepts to ensure precision in indexing.', 'combination': 'Combine MeSH and free-text terms with OR for each concept block and AND between blocks to balance sensitivity and specificity.'}, 'additional_caveats': {'timeframe': 'Consider limiting to recent years (e.g., post-2010) given the rapid evolution of optogenetic tools and memory research.', 'animal models': 'Explicitly exclude studies using non-rodent models (e.g., non-mammalian species) unless specified otherwise.', 'human studies': 'Exclude human studies unless the question explicitly includes them, as optogenetic techniques are not yet widely used in humans.'}}

map.notes: {'scope': 'The search focuses on studies explicitly analyzing microglia in Alzheimer’s disease using single-cell RNA sequencing or related omics methods. It includes both traditional and emerging techniques like spatial transcriptomics and advanced bioinformatics tools.', 'ambiguity': 'Ensure exclusion of studies on other cell types or non-Alzheimer’s disease contexts to avoid overlap. For spatial transcriptomics, consider filtering by brain tissue specificity to avoid including non-brain samples.', 'caveats': ["Some studies may use broader terms like 'neuroinflammation' or 'immune response' without explicitly mentioning microglia or single-cell RNA sequencing. These should be captured via the free-text terms.", "Newer techniques like 'spatial transcriptomics' and 'multi-omics' may not yet have MeSH terms, so free-text terms are critical for capturing these.", 'Ensure inclusion of both preclinical (animal) and clinical (human) studies to capture diverse perspectives.']}

It includes both traditional and emerging techniques like spatial transcriptomics and advanced bioinformatics tools.', 'ambiguity': 'Ensure exclusion of studies on other cell types or non-Alzheimer’s disease contexts to avoid overlap. For spatial transcriptomics, consider filtering by brain tissue specificity to avoid including non-brain samples.', 'caveats': ["Some studies may use broader terms like 'neuroinflammation' or 'immune response' without explicitly mentioning microglia or single-cell RNA sequencing. These should be captured via the free-text terms.", "Newer techniques like 'spatial transcriptomics' and 'multi-omics' may not yet have MeSH terms, so free-text terms are critical for capturing these.", 'Ensure inclusion of both preclinical (animal) and clinical (human) studies to capture diverse perspectives.']}

concepts.name: Population
concepts.rationale: Captures studies involving genome/genomic data relevant to CRISPR off-target effects, ensuring broad inclusion of genetic and genomic research.

concepts.name: Intervention/Exposure
concepts.rationale: Covers all CRISPR-Cas9 and related systems, ensuring broad capture of the intervention/exposure of interest, including newer or emerging CRISPR variants.

concepts.name: Outcome
concepts.rationale: Captures all aspects of off-target effects, including mutations, genomic instability, and computational/detection methods, ensuring broad recall of outcomes related to CRISPR off-target effects.

concepts.name: Method
concepts.rationale: Captures all bioinformatics, computational, and methodological approaches to detecting CRISPR off-target effects, including emerging tools like deep learning, machine learning, and specialized CRISPR-specific algorithms.

map.notes: {'scope': 'The search is designed to maximize recall by including both MeSH terms and a wide array of free-text terms that cover current jargon, abbreviations, and methodological variations. It intentionally avoids overly restrictive qualifiers to ensure broad coverage of the literature.', 'ambiguity': {'method': "Some terms like 'bioinformatics tools' or 'computational methods' could overlap with broader genomic studies. To mitigate this, the free-text terms are heavily focused on CRISPR-specific off-target detection methods, computational pipelines, and bioinformatics tools dedicated to CRISPR analysis.", 'outcome': "The inclusion of 'genomic instability' and 'genomic alterations' alongside 'off-target effects' ensures that studies reporting effects beyond direct mutations are captured. However, some studies might use these terms loosely; a post-hoc filtering step could refine results to focus strictly on off-target effects detection methods."}, 'reproducibility': {'suggestions': ['Consider using Boolean operators (AND, OR) to combine these concept blocks in a structured search string (e.g., `Population OR Exposure OR Outcome OR Method`).', 'For MeSH terms, use the exact canonical headings provided. For free-text terms, ensure they are combined with the `tiab` (title/abstract) operator in PubMed search syntax.', "To avoid redundancy, consider using the `NOT` operator to exclude terms like 'gene editing' or 'genome editing' if the focus is strictly on off-target detection methods (though this may reduce recall)."]}}

concepts.name: Population
concepts.rationale: The population of interest is rodents, specifically mice and rats, which are commonly used in neuroscience research.

concepts.name: Intervention/Exposure
concepts.rationale: The intervention involves optogenetic techniques, which use light to control neurons that have been genetically modified to express light-sensitive ion channels.

concepts.name: Target Area
concepts.rationale: The specific brain region targeted by the optogenetic intervention is the hippocampus, known for its role in memory consolidation.

concepts.name: Outcome
concepts.rationale: The outcome of interest is the improvement in memory consolidation, a process by which short-term memories are stabilized into long-term storage.

map.notes: The search strategy aims to capture studies involving optogenetic stimulation of the hippocampus in rodent models and assesses their impact on memory consolidation. The focus is on high recall, so synonyms and related terms are included to ensure comprehensive coverage. concepts.rationale: The intervention involves optogenetic techniques, which use light to control neurons that have been genetically modified to express light-sensitive ion channels.

concepts.name: Target Area
concepts.rationale: The specific brain region targeted by the optogenetic intervention is the hippocampus, known for its role in memory consolidation.

concepts.name: Outcome
concepts.rationale: The outcome of interest is the improvement in memory consolidation, a process by which short-term memories are stabilized into long-term storage.

map.notes: The search strategy aims to capture studies involving optogenetic stimulation of the hippocampus in rodent models and assesses their impact on memory consolidation. The focus is on high recall, so synonyms and related terms are included to ensure comprehensive coverage. The scope is limited to rodent models, which are the most common subjects in this type of research.

map.notes: The search strategy aims to capture a wide range of studies by including both MeSH terms and free-text synonyms. The field of single-cell RNA sequencing is rapidly evolving, so it is important to include the latest jargon and methodological terms. The scope is limited to studies that specifically address microglia in the context of Alzheimer's disease using single-cell RNA sequencing techniques.

concepts.name: Method
concepts.rationale: This block includes the methods used to analyze the data obtained from single-cell RNA sequencing, emphasizing current jargon in bioinformatics and computational biology.

map.notes: The search strategy aims to capture a wide range of studies by including both MeSH terms and free-text synonyms. The field of single-cell RNA sequencing is rapidly evolving, so it is important to include the latest jargon and methodological terms. The scope is limited to studies that specifically address microglia in the context of Alzheimer's disease using single-cell RNA sequencing techniques.

concepts.name: Microglial cells
concepts.rationale: Understanding the role of microglia in Alzheimer's disease is crucial for developing effective therapeutic strategies. Single-cell RNA sequencing can provide insights into microglial activation, heterogeneity, and function in this context.
freetext: Microglial activation, neuroinflammation, and immune response in Alzheimer's disease.
Single-cell RNA sequencing of microglia in Alzheimer's disease.
Microglial heterogeneity, single-cell analysis, and biomarker discovery in AD.

concepts.name: Alzheimer's disease
concepts.rationale: Understanding the underlying mechanisms of Alzheimer's disease is essential for developing effective treatments. Single-cell RNA sequencing can provide insights into the complex interactions between microglia and other cells in this context.
freetext: Alzheimer's disease is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by amyloid-beta accumulation and tau protein phosphorylation.
The pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease involves multiple cellular and molecular mechanisms, including microglial activation and immune response.

concepts.name: Single-cell RNA sequencing
concepts.rationale: Single-cell RNA sequencing can provide insights into the transcriptomic profiles of microglia in Alzheimer's disease, allowing for a more comprehensive understanding of their function and behavior.
freetext: Single-cell RNA sequencing is a powerful tool for analyzing the transcriptome of individual cells.
The use of single-cell RNA sequencing has revolutionized our understanding of cellular heterogeneity and diversity in complex tissues like the brain.

map.notes: The use of single-cell RNA sequencing in Alzheimer's disease research is still in its early stages. Further studies are needed to validate these findings and identify potential therapeutic targets.
